what: HF Sinclair refines crude oil into fuels, markets them through Sinclair branded stations, produces renewable diesel, makes lubricants and specialty products, and owns midstream assets.
customers: Fuel wholesalers and branded station operators in the western United States, plus lubricant and specialty product buyers.
money: seven refineries in the Rockies, Southwest and Mid-Continent
Sinclair branded fuel and Petro-Canada lubricants
moat: Refineries in inland western markets that are insulated from Gulf Coast competition by transport costs, combined with its own branded retail outlets.
risks: Refining margins drive earnings and are outside its control
Revenue has fallen about 11% a year over three years
Renewable diesel economics depend on government credits
Refineries need periodic expensive maintenance shutdowns
opportunities: Analysts see about 35% upside from current levels
Cash of about $3.3 billion roughly matches its debt
Lubricants and specialty products earn steadier margins than refining
watch: Refining margin per barrel and renewable diesel profitability.
